arenas.title: The Growth Gauntlet
arenas.theme: Conversion, creative tests and demand generation
arenas.core_proof: TCS loan-offer conversion increased from 1.5% to 2.4% (+60% relative) through placement/copy A/B tests; TCS CRM 10% holdouts demonstrated ₹12 Cr incremental annual card spend; HABER action-led CTR 10.73% vs 7.01% across creative testing.
arenas.hero_problem: A fast-growing campaign has clicks, but the team must establish whether engagement and conversion are real.

hero_moves.title: Budget Blast
hero_moves.decision: Spend more before checking conversion quality
hero_moves.reaction: Budget Beast gets bigger. Spending does not substitute for experiment and funnel diagnosis.
hero_moves.learning: Diagnose metric definition, qualified conversion and experiment validity first.

hero_moves.title: Experiment Lens
hero_moves.decision: Audit baseline, audience, creative tests and conversion funnel before reallocating spend
hero_moves.reaction: Critical hit! Shivam uses creative testing and conversion analysis to decide what to test next.
hero_moves.learning: Distinguish CTR, CPC, conversion rate, CAC and actual revenue.

hero_moves.title: CTR Confetti
hero_moves.decision: Declare success solely because CTR increased
hero_moves.reaction: The monster shrugs. CTR does not prove revenue or customer retention.
hero_moves.learning: Connect creative performance to qualified outcomes.

arenas.title: The Insight Illusion
arenas.theme: Firsthand research and realistic market planning
arenas.core_proof: TCS analyzed 50,000 under-30 customer records and 12 interviews to reposition savings accounts, increasing openings 45%; Parle fieldwork covered 29 stores and a four-lever GTM plan; HABER identified a 92.7% brand-led search discovery gap.

hero_moves.title: Assumption Arrow
hero_moves.decision: Set a nationwide strategy using only gut feel
hero_moves.reaction: Monster dodges. Without observed user behavior, a strategy may solve the wrong problem.
hero_moves.learning: Start with observed problem and a research sample.

hero_moves.title: Customer Radar
hero_moves.decision: Observe real behavior, segment the data, and label proposals versus observed results
hero_moves.reaction: Critical hit! Field research reveals retailer choice is not the same as a stockout.
hero_moves.learning: Validate who is making the decision and why.

hero_moves.title: Forecast Fireworks
hero_moves.decision: Celebrate future KPI targets as if they have already been achieved
hero_moves.reaction: The monster points at the calendar. Targets are not realized results.
hero_moves.learning: Separate baseline, forecast, test and measured outcome.

arenas.title: The Ownership Arena
arenas.core_proof: ThinkQuota MVP shipped in about four weeks; Target Cart Recovery AI Agent project reduced AI calls per decision 8→1 and met all tested workflow gates in nine scenarios; TCS SME lending module launch added ₹40 Cr pipeline over two quarters.

hero_moves.title: Infinite Deck
hero_moves.decision: Create another elaborate strategy deck without shipping anything
hero_moves.reaction: The AI Fog King summons an even bigger deck.
hero_moves.learning: Define the smallest working product and measurable acceptance tests.

hero_moves.title: MVP Forge
hero_moves.decision: Ship the minimal product, enforce safety gates and test the workflow

hero_moves.title: Revenue Illusion
hero_moves.decision: Assume nine successful workflow tests prove incremental sales
hero_moves.reaction: The monster laughs. Lab tests do not establish production revenue.
hero_moves.learning: Run a holdout and measure incremental outcomes when deployed.

father_attacks.name: The 60% Conversion Trap
father_attacks.question: You improved in-app loan-offer conversion by 60%. Was that a 60-percentage-point jump? What did you actually change?
father_attacks.answer: At TCS, I A/B tested placement and copy for pre-approved in-app loan offers. Conversion rose from 1.5% to 2.4%: a 0.9-percentage-point increase and a 60% relative lift. I changed how and where the offer appeared, then used conversion performance to judge the test.
father_attacks.evidence: TCS: in-app loan offer conversion 1.5% → 2.4%, +60% relative, via placement and copy A/B testing.
father_attacks.limitation: The 60% is a relative increase, not 60 percentage points. This result is specific to the tested loan offer, not every banking product.
father_attacks.learning: For the next experiment, track qualified outcomes beyond the initial offer conversion.
father_attacks.papa: Wah beta! Percent aur percentage point ka chakkar bhi clear hai. Counterattack successful!
father_attacks.source: Latest CV — TCS loan-offer conversion bullet
father_attacks.supporting_material_suggestion: Optional proof drawer: original test setup and metric breakdown

father_attacks.name: The ₹12 Crore Holdout Challenge
father_attacks.question: Marketing teams always take credit for sales. How did you establish that CRM actually generated incremental card spending?
father_attacks.answer: At TCS, I used 10% holdout groups to measure the incremental contribution of CRM. The analysis showed ₹12 crore in incremental annual card spend, and I retired four low-performing campaigns based on the evidence.
father_attacks.evidence: TCS: 10% CRM holdout groups; ₹12 Cr incremental annual card spend; 4 low-performing campaigns retired.
father_attacks.limitation: Incremental card spend is not the same metric as profit or bank revenue. The holdout was the basis for incrementality measurement.
father_attacks.learning: Continue testing long-term lift and profitability before scaling further.
father_attacks.papa: Control group bhi? Yeh toh asli marketing science ka jaadu hai!
father_attacks.source: Latest CV — TCS CRM incremental spend bullet
father_attacks.supporting_material_suggestion: Optional: show a relevant CV/project extract if available

father_attacks.name: The Retail Reality Check
father_attacks.question: You can look at dashboards. But have you actually investigated what happens on the ground?
father_attacks.power: Retail Field Research: Ground Reality Radar
father_attacks.answer: In my Parle-G field-sales and GTM project, I audited 29 GT and MT outlets, assessed assortment and POSM, identified that 31% of the observed shelves lacked Parle-G and that two-thirds of those absences came from retailer choice rather than stockouts. I developed a four-lever GTM plan and also identified higher margins where outlets stocked five or more packs.
father_attacks.evidence: Parle: 29 GT/MT outlets; 31% of shelves lacked Parle-G; about two-thirds due to retailer choice; 10.25% margin with 5+ packs vs 8.67% for single-pack outlets; four-lever GTM plan.
father_attacks.limitation: The research covers 29 audited outlets; the four-lever plan is a proposed strategy, not a claimed nationwide realized sales result.
father_attacks.learning: Validate the retailer-insight pattern in additional stores before broader rollout.
father_attacks.papa: Bas Excel mein nahi, dukaan mein bhi research ki! Bahut badhiya.
father_attacks.supporting_material_suggestion: Optional: show a relevant CV/project extract if available

father_attacks.name: The Show-Me-What-You-Built Attack
father_attacks.question: Enough strategy decks! What have you actually built, and what trade-offs did you make?
father_attacks.answer: I scoped and shipped the ThinkQuota MVP in roughly four weeks, including live AI, an attempt gate, prompt budget and faculty dashboard. I deliberately cut a streak feature to protect the core experience. Separately, in the Cart Recovery AI Agent project I built enforced decision guardrails and reduced AI calls from eight to one per decision.
father_attacks.evidence: ThinkQuota: MVP shipped in ~4 weeks, streak feature removed. Cart Recovery AI Agent project: AI calls 8 → 1; workflow rules met fatigue, complaint-risk and margin gates across 9 tests.
father_attacks.limitation: The AI Agent results refer to the project’s nine test scenarios, not an asserted production rollout. ThinkQuota’s pilot economics are modeled separately from the MVP shipping result.
father_attacks.learning: Keep testing real user activation after shipping and broaden edge-case coverage.
father_attacks.papa: Ek taraf MVP ship kiya, doosri taraf AI cost kam ki. Yeh hui na ownership!

father_attacks.name: The ₹40 Crore Pipeline Ambush
father_attacks.question: You say you added ₹40 crore to the lending pipeline. Does that mean the bank earned ₹40 crore in revenue?
father_attacks.answer: At TCS, I orchestrated an SME lending module launch across presales, delivery and account teams, adding ₹40 crore to the pipeline over two quarters. That is a real pipeline result. It does not mean ₹40 crore was booked as bank revenue or disbursed as loans. Separately, I helped guide a ₹10 crore budget shift using a marketing mix model built on three years of data from seven channels, improving return on spend by 12%.
father_attacks.evidence: TCS: ₹40 Cr added to SME lending pipeline in 2 quarters; ₹10 Cr budget shift informed by 3 years of MMM data across 7 channels; return on spend +12%.
father_attacks.limitation: Pipeline, disbursed principal, profit and revenue are different measures; the question’s revenue interpretation is too broad. The precise accomplishments remain true.
father_attacks.learning: Track pipeline stage progression and realized value alongside growth of the initial opportunity pipeline.

choices.label: Content Creators
choices.hypothesis: Creators who draft scripts, captions and AI prompts may find spoken-first drafting useful.
choices.pilot: Recruit a small relevant creator cohort, demonstrate real before/after workflows, and compare activated users to viewers or referrals.
choices.measure: Signup-to-first-successful-dictation activation, weekly active usage, D7 retention and cost per retained user.
choices.risk: A viral video can attract curiosity without habitual product use.

choices.label: Students
choices.hypothesis: Some students may prefer speaking initial notes, assignments or AI prompts, if the product fits their workflow.
choices.pilot: Test campus workshops and ambassador referrals with real tasks, then interview retained and churned users.
choices.measure: Activation, repeat weekly dictation, D7 retention and referral conversion.
choices.risk: High trial volume may conceal low willingness to adopt the habit.

choices.label: Startup Founders
choices.hypothesis: Busy founders who frequently context-switch may value speaking long instructions into the tools they already use.
choices.pilot: Run a small workflow-based cohort test around emails, notes and AI prompts; compare follow-through after onboarding.
choices.measure: First-week activation, repeat usage, qualitative time saved, cost per activated user.
choices.risk: A compelling demo may not survive daily task switching and privacy concerns.

attack_outcomes.partial: Relevant real resume power is available, but the Father’s question overstates or conflates what the true achievement measures; no heart loss.

game_rules.repeat_attacks: Do not deduct a heart twice for the same attack in the same run.
game_rules.arena_completion: At least one question or move resolved AND the mandatory core-proof spotlight viewed in that arena. Optional additional attacks remain accessible.
game_rules.father_path: Choose questions and challenge evidence; can select 'Show proof' or 'Not convinced', where latter opens a deeper limitation. Do not auto-endorse unsupported results.
game_rules.shivam_path: Choose one of three skills per arena; weak move loses one heart once per arena/move and offers meaningful retry; correct move unlocks same proof spotlight.
game_rules.zero_hearts: Trigger Infinite Learner Comeback animation; preserve journal and previous losses; restore one playable heart and allow continuation, never softlock or pretend gaps are completed accomplishments.
game_rules.finale_unlock: All three arena core-proof spotlights viewed; may reach ending with gaps still in journal.
game_rules.ending: Fictional shortlisted, not an actual hiring offer.

game_rules.core_proof_requires_truthfulness: Treat latest CV facts as true and present them directly. Keep accurate meanings of achieved outcomes, future targets, modeled scenarios and project test results.
game_rules.resume_vault: Make all 21 resume powers discoverable. Treat completed CV achievements as true; distinguish future targets, model projections, and classroom/project tests as described.
